tasks.short: Write technical documents and academic articles communicating findings and forecasts

steps.what: Check study results, forecast versions and sources for the technical document
Write the article outline and specify findings and limitations to communicate
Write the technical document or academic article prose

loop.purpose: Draft technical prose from selected findings and the economist's argument
loop.input: Communication brief, result tables, forecast version and real references
loop.check: Economist checks every result, forecast condition, causal claim and limitation against the actual analysis
loop.stop: One correction then manual writing for unsupported or changed economic meaning
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot express the particular study argument

steps.what: Format the technical article and its tables and references
Check and finish the technical article
Send the final technical document to the internal research team

tasks.design: Use a bounded drafting loop and native formatting templates in {DOCS} for the selected results and forecast narrative. The economist checks the finished document and separately sends the exact final version through {EMAIL} to the internal research team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prose and formatting repeat work after findings and the communication argument are settled.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting and native styles can assist those writing fragments.
tasks.still_hard: Forecast conditions and uncertainty must not become unsupported certainty in the prose.
tasks.human_edge: The economist chooses the argument and understands the limits of the study.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated prose and formatting; responsibility for findings stays unchanged.

reach.task: Trace each reported result to its source table

evidence.claim: Source-bound drafting and native document formatting can assist technical economic writing; the combined time estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes source checking, argument capture, writing, formatting, finishing and an internal research-team handoff. Journal submission is a later publication action not performed by this design.

The research workflow produces actual study results or forecast outputs. The economist checks source, release version and table in s1 and captures claim, caveat, reference and audience in s2 at full time; no ready-made manuscript is assumed.
The native formatter consumes s3 text and the existing template. Missing references or conflicting forecast versions return to manual writing and formatting; no invented citation is accepted.
Test native templates and reference tools first. Formatting savings require current manual formatting; same-system saves earn no saving or self-gate.
research_questions: Can checked drafting preserve every forecast condition while reducing prose time?

already_counted.description: Brief capture, draft correction, final content checks and handoff checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain document templates and inspect source-bound drafting errors.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final document, tables, references and internal research recipients checked before s6 send; any change voids the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R67.5, gross32.5 minus6 upkeep gives net26.5. Range8-18 assumes real manual prose and formatting remain; all economic interpretation and final checking stay human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define the economic and environmental research question and inclusion criteria
Find economic and environmental literature and source records
Screen research records for relevance to the economic and environmental question

loop.purpose: Prioritize candidate records for researcher screening
loop.input: Real catalogue records, inclusion criteria and researcher relevance labels
loop.output: Ranked screening queue with source identifiers
loop.check: Economist reads candidate sources and checks sampled low-ranked records for missed relevant environmental or economic evidence
loop.stop: An agreed bounded review set; uncertain recall or topic drift returns the remaining records to manual screening
loop.why_not_simpler: Keywords alone miss topic relevance expressed in different terms; the model prioritizes and never decides inclusion

steps.what: Assess methods and implications in the selected environmental research
Write research notes describing findings, gaps and limitations

tasks.design: Use saved searches in the {OTHER} research catalogue and a bounded ranking loop to prioritize real candidate sources. The economist decides inclusion, appraises methods and writes findings and gaps in {DOCS}; ranking does not create research evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated search setup and screening large result sets consume time before appraisal.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches and relevance-ranking tools can assist discovery and prioritization.
tasks.still_hard: Weak studies and context-dependent results still require expert appraisal.
tasks.human_edge: The economist identifies a gap or flawed inference despite apparently relevant wording.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive search and screening; appraisal and conclusions stay human.

reach.task: Clarify the context behind an environmental research result

evidence.claim: ASReview prioritizes literature records for screening; this supports a ranked queue, not automatic inclusion, appraisal or the proposed savings.

assumptions: Scenario covers the literature and evidence-research phase. Empirical collection and alternative-comparison analysis belong to task16910 when the same study needs them, and must be counted there once rather than silently omitted from a team roll-up.

The economist writes the question and criteria in s1. Candidate id, title, abstract and source location come from the catalogue; the economist checks records in s2 and produces relevance labels during s3 screening, with that time retained.
Missing abstracts, unreliable identifiers or poor ranking cause manual screening. There is no assumed prelabelled corpus, free relevance score or automatic exclusion decision.
Test native saved searches, deduplication and filters before ranking. No saving is assigned to appraisal or actual research-note writing.
unknowns: Typical search volume and available abstracts
research_questions: Does ranked screening find relevant sources with less effort after labels and low-ranked sampling are counted?

already_counted.description: Relevance labels, source checking and low-ranked sampling remain in screening time.

incremental.description: Maintain searches and inspect missed-source patterns after topic changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R88.5, gross11.5 minus4 upkeep gives net7.5. Range1-4 assumes sizable recurrent searches where prioritization helps; expert appraisal and written findings retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect and analyze data comparing environmental policy alternatives

steps.what: Define policy alternatives, environmental measures and comparison assumptions
Collect environmental and economic data and verify their provenance
Align data units, periods and geography using specified transformations
Calculate environmental implications for each policy or practice alternative
Analyze the environmental differences and test interpretation limits
Record the environmental comparison findings and limitations

tasks.design: Configure native transformations and scenario calculations in {SPREADSHEET} from the economist's explicit comparison specification. The economist collects and checks sources, reviews transformations, interprets the differences and records actual findings in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated alignment and scenario arithmetic consume time after comparison choices are made.
tasks.enabler_now: Native data transformations and reusable formulas can reproduce specified comparisons.
tasks.still_hard: Data from different periods or boundaries may not be comparable.
tasks.human_edge: The economist detects when an apparently precise comparison is invalid.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat transformation and calculation; appraisal of environmental implications stays human.

evidence.claim: Native transformations and scenario formulas can support specified environmental comparisons without a model; the time estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes comparison design, actual data collection and checking, alignment, calculations, interpretation and the findings record. No structured dataset is supplied for free.
The economist captures measure, value, unit, period, geography, source and release version in s2 and specifies alternative, boundary and allowed transformation in s1. Their capture time is full.

s3 applies only explicitly specified unit and period transformations; the economist checks results and handles ambiguous mappings in retained time. s4 produces scenario results only after that review.

Missing definitions or incompatible boundaries stop formulas for manual analysis. Test native data transformations and formulas first. Existing scripted calculations and internal saves earn no new labour saving.
unknowns: Actual data comparability and revision frequency
research_questions: Do native transformations reproduce manually checked comparisons without extra source cleaning?

already_counted.description: Data collection, transformation checking, interpretation and findings capture remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain source mappings and test scenario formulas after revisions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R74, gross26 minus7 upkeep gives net19. Range5-12 assumes repeat transformations and arithmetic remain manual; source appraisal and environmental judgement retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess environmental and natural-resource costs and benefits of policies and activities

steps.what: Define cost-benefit boundaries, valuation methods and environmental alternatives
Collect and check valuation inputs, costs, benefits and resource changes
Calculate costs, benefits and sensitivities for the specified alternatives
Assess cost-benefit results, distributional effects and unpriced impacts
Write and check the cost-benefit assessment explanation

loop.purpose: Express the economist's assessment and limitations
loop.input: Assessment notes and verified scenario tables
loop.output: Editable assessment prose with table references
loop.check: Economist checks valuation assumptions, distributional effects, nonmonetary impacts and uncertainty against the actual assessment
loop.stop: One correction then manual explanation if values or conclusions are distorted
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot express the economist's particular appraisal

tasks.design: Use native {SPREADSHEET} sensitivity tables for the economist's specified valuations and alternatives. A bounded {DOCS} loop assists the assessment explanation; method selection, source checking, distributional judgement and unpriced impacts remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated scenario arithmetic and explanation writing add time around the appraisal.
tasks.enabler_now: Native sensitivity tables and source-bound drafting can assist those fragments.
tasks.still_hard: Valuation methods and nonmonetary environmental effects involve contested choices.
tasks.human_edge: The economist makes assumptions explicit and prevents a monetary total from concealing important impacts.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat calculation and prose; assessment authority remains unchanged.

reach.task: Identify ecological impacts that a monetary assessment misses

evidence.claim: Native sensitivity tables and checked model prose can support cost-benefit documentation without selecting valuations or policy; the estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes assessment scope, actual valuation-data capture, calculations, judgement and the written explanation. Physical environmental comparisons from task16910 are reused once if the same project uses them, while monetary valuation and assessment work remain here.

The economist produces affected group, period, quantity, valuation source, unit, price basis, discount assumption and scenario bound in s1 and s2 with full time retained. No free priced-impact list or preferred-policy flag is assumed.

s3 produces scenario tables from the checked inputs; missing valuations, double-counting concerns or unresolved methods return to manual assessment. s4 produces the actual judgement notes consumed by the model.
Test native scenario tables and document templates first. Existing automatic arithmetic earns no saving, and internal assessment saves require no invented self-approval.
unknowns: Availability and applicability of valuation sources
research_questions: Can repeated scenario calculations save time after valuation choices and source checks remain fully counted?

already_counted.description: Valuation capture, assessment notes and checked explanation writing remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain valuation-source links and test scenario tables after changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R75.5, gross24.5 minus6 upkeep gives net18.5. Range4-10 assumes recurring scenario arithmetic and some checked prose help; valuation judgement and actual assessment notes retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Environmental economic judgement remains human while selected screening, repeat calculations and technical prose become shorter.
reach: Check measurement boundaries with environmental scientists
Identify unpriced ecological effects with conservation scientists
skills_to_grow: Keep valuation assumptions and uncertainty visible
role.ambitious_version: An economist who can trace environmental policy claims to evidence and assumptions with less repetitive calculation and writing.
